label: Rennet occurs in all multi-stomached animals and, among others, in the hare
claim: Rennet is found in all animals with a multiple stomach and, among single-stomached animals, in the hare.
quote: What is known as rennet is found in all animals that have a multiple stomach, and in the hare among animals whose stomach is single.

label: Vipers and selachians produce eggs internally and bear live young
claim: Vipers among serpents, like the selachians (cartilaginous fishes) among fishes, first produce eggs internally and then bring forth live young.
quote: For both these and vipers are externally viviparous, but previously produce ova internally.

label: All fishes have a gall-bladder, mostly attached to the intestine
claim: All fishes have a gall-bladder, and in most of them it is attached to the intestine rather than to the liver.
quote: For all fishes have a gall-bladder; and in most of them it is attached to the intestine

label: Horse, mule, ass, deer and roe have no gall-bladder
claim: Some animals have no gall-bladder at all, among them the horse, mule, ass, deer and roe; the camel has only small biliary vessels, and the seal and dolphin have none.
quote: For in some animals there is absolutely no gall-bladder at all--in the horse, for instance, the mule, the ass, the deer, and the roe
scope: horse, mule, ass, deer, roe deer, camel, seal, dolphin

label: Gall-bladder size in sheep and goats varies by locality
claim: Sheep and goats usually have a gall-bladder, but in some localities (Naxos) it is enormously large and in others (a district of Chalcis in Euboea) it is altogether absent.
quote: For these animals usually have a gall-bladder; but, while in some localities it is so enormously big as to appear a monstrosity, as is the case in Naxos, in others it is altogether wanting
scope: sheep and goats in different localities

label: Animals without a gall-bladder are long-lived
claim: Animals without a gall-bladder, such as deer, solid-hoofed animals, the camel and the dolphin, are long-lived.
quote: For such have no gall-bladder and live long. But besides these there are other animals that have no gall-bladder, though those old writers had not noticed the fact, such as the camel and the dolphin; and these also are, as it happens, long-lived.
scope: mammals with and without a gall-bladder: deer, horse, ass, camel, dolphin

label: All cephalopods have ink, the cuttlefish most
claim: All cephalopods have ink, and the cuttlefish (Sepia) has more of it than any other.
quote: All Cephalopoda alike have this characteristic ink, but chief of all the Sepia, where it is more abundant than in the rest.

label: Crayfish and some crabs have a second set of teeth in the stomach
claim: In the Carabi (spiny lobsters and the like) and some crabs the stomach has a second set of teeth, because the front teeth are not enough to chew the food properly.
quote: and then a stomach, which in the Carabi and some of the Crabs is furnished with a second set of teeth, the anterior teeth being insufficient for adequate mastication.
scope: decapod crustaceans: Carabi (spiny lobsters, crayfish) and crabs

label: Sea-urchin 'eggs' grow largest at full moon
claim: The so-called eggs of sea-urchins become larger than usual at the time of the full moon, because the nights are then warmer from the moonlight, not because the urchins eat more.
quote: yet they acquire a greater size than usual at the time of full moon; not, as some think, because sea-urchins eat more at that season, but because the nights are then warmer, owing to the moonlight.

label: Every sea-urchin has five 'eggs', five teeth and five stomachs
claim: The number of so-called eggs is the same in all sea-urchins and is odd: five, matching their five teeth and five stomach compartments.
quote: The number of the ova is the same in all sea-urchins, and is an odd one. For there are five ova, just as there are also five teeth and five stomachs

label: Nature passes from lifeless things to animals by unbroken gradation
claim: Nature passes from lifeless things to animals in an unbroken sequence, with living things that are not animals between them, so that neighbouring groups scarcely differ.
quote: For nature passes from lifeless objects to animals in such unbroken sequence, interposing between them beings which live and yet are not animals, that scarcely any difference seems to exist between two neighbouring groups owing to their close proximity.
scope: all living things: plants, sponges, ascidians, animals

label: Cicadas live on moisture deposited from the air
claim: Cicadas find enough to live on in the moisture deposited from the air, insects in general being small eaters because of their cold nature.
quote: In no insects is this so conspicuous as in these Cicadae. For they find enough to live on in the moisture which is deposited from the air.

label: Very small flying insects have only two wings
claim: Flying insects that are very small have only two wings, as flies do, while larger ones such as bees have four.
quote: When, however, such insects are of very small bulk, their feathers are reduced to two, as is the case with flies.
scope: flying insects: Diptera versus Hymenoptera and others

label: In crabs and spiny lobsters the right claw is always the larger
claim: In the Carabi (spiny lobsters and crayfish) and in crabs the right claw is invariably the larger and stronger; only in the lobster is it a matter of chance which claw is larger.
quote: In the Carabi and in the Crabs the right claw is invariably the larger and the stronger.
scope: decapod crustaceans with claws: crabs, Carabi; lobsters (Astaci) as the stated exception

label: All cephalopods have eight feet, short in cuttlefish and squid, long in octopus
claim: All cephalopods have eight feet, which are short in cuttlefish and squid and longer in the octopus.
quote: Again, though the number of feet is the same in all the Cephalopoda, namely eight, their length varies in different kinds, being short in the Sepias and the Calamaries, but greater in the Poulps.

label: Wolves and lions have a neck made of a single bone
claim: In all other animals the neck is flexible and has several vertebrae, but in wolves and lions it consists of a single bone.
quote: In all other animals this neck is flexible and contains several vertebrae; but in wolves and lions it contains only a single bone.
scope: wolves and lions versus other animals with a neck

label: Foals are nearly as tall as grown horses, with relatively long legs
claim: In solid- and cloven-hoofed quadrupeds the lower parts are largest in youth, so that foals are scarcely shorter than full-grown horses and can touch their heads with their hind legs, which adults cannot.
quote: Thus it is that colts are scarcely, if at all, below full-grown horses in height; and that while still young they can touch their heads with the hind legs, though this is no longer possible when they are older.
scope: horses and other hoofed quadrupeds; contrasted with human children, whose upper parts are largest

label: Man has hands because he is intelligent, not intelligent because he has hands
claim: Man does not owe his superior intelligence to his hands, as Anaxagoras held; he has hands because he is the most intelligent animal, nature giving each organ to the animal that can use it.
quote: we must conclude that man does not owe his superior intelligence to his hands, but his hands to his superior intelligence.

label: Wolves, lions, dogs and leopards have five front toes and four hind
claim: Some polydactylous quadrupeds, such as wolves, lions, dogs and leopards, have five digits on each forefoot but only four on each hind foot.
quote: It is this hand-like office of the anterior limbs which explains why in some of the polydactylous quadrupeds, such as wolves, lions, dogs, and leopards, there are actually five digits on each forefoot, though there are only four on each hind one.

label: Mammae: two at the thighs in animals with few young, many on the belly in litter-bearers
claim: Animals that bear few young at a time, whether horned or solid-hoofed, have two mammae in the region of the thighs, while litter-bearing or polydactylous animals have numerous teats along the belly or two in the middle of the abdomen.
quote: Thus in such animals as produce but few at a birth, whether horned quadrupeds or those with solid hoofs, the mammae are placed in the region of the thighs, and are two in number, while in such as produce litters, or such as are polydactylous, the dugs are either numerous and placed laterally on the belly, as in swine and dogs
scope: viviparous quadrupeds: horse, ass, camel, deer, ox, goat, swine, dog, lion

label: All female quadrupeds urinate backwards; only a few males do
claim: All female quadrupeds urinate backwards, while among males only a few do so, such as the lynx, lion, camel and hare; no solid-hoofed quadruped urinates backwards.
quote: All female quadrupeds void their urine backwards, because the position of the parts which this implies is useful to them in the act of copulation. This is the case with only some few males, such as the lynx, the lion, the camel, and the hare.

label: Man alone lacks a tail and alone has buttocks
claim: Man has no tail but has buttocks, which no quadruped has; the nourishment that would go to a tail goes to the buttocks and fleshy legs that upright posture requires.
quote: But man is tail-less. He has, however, buttocks, which exist in none of the quadrupeds.
scope: man versus quadrupeds; the ape as intermediate

label: Huckle-bones occur mostly in cloven-hoofed animals, never in many-toed ones
claim: No polydactylous quadruped has a huckle-bone (astragalus), solid-hoofed animals as a rule lack one, and most animals that have one are cloven-hoofed.
quote: As to the polydactylous quadrupeds, none of them have huckle-bones. For if they had they would not be polydactylous, but the divisions of the foot would only extend to that amount of its breadth which was covered by the huckle-bone. Thus it is that most of the animals that have huckle-bones are cloven-hoofed.

label: The river crocodile alone among these animals has no tongue
claim: All oviparous quadrupeds and serpents have a tongue in the mouth except the river crocodile, which has only a space where a tongue would be.
quote: and in all, with the single exception of the river crocodile, there is a tongue inside the mouth.
scope: oviparous quadrupeds and serpents; the Nile crocodile

label: Oviparous quadrupeds have no upper eyelid and close the eye with the lower
claim: Oviparous quadrupeds have no upper eyelid and close the eye with the lower lid, as birds do.
quote: These animals have no upper eyelid, but close the eye with the lower lid In this they resemble birds
scope: oviparous quadrupeds (lizards, tortoises, crocodiles) and birds

label: The crocodile moves its upper jaw rather than its lower
claim: In all other animals it is the lower jaw that moves, but in the river crocodile it is the upper jaw.
quote: While in all other animals it is the lower jaw that is movable, in the river crocodile it is exceptionally the upper.
scope: the Nile crocodile versus other animals

label: No animal that is not internally viviparous has milk or mammae
claim: No animal that is not internally viviparous has milk or mammae, so birds, fishes, oviparous quadrupeds and serpents have none; in them the nourishment corresponding to milk is formed in the egg.
quote: This absence of milk is not peculiar to these animals, but is common to all such as are not internally viviparous.

label: Long-legged birds have long necks, except web-footed birds
claim: In birds the length of the neck as a rule follows that of the legs, long-legged birds having long necks and short-legged birds short ones, with web-footed birds as the exception.
quote: For long-legged birds have a long neck, short-legged birds a short one, to which rule, however, the web-footed birds form an exception.

label: Spurs and talons never co-occur in the same bird
claim: No bird has both spurs and talons; spurs belong to heavy ground birds and talons to birds of prey.
quote: Spurs and talons never co-exist in the same bird. For nature never makes anything superfluous
scope: birds: Galliformes and other spurred birds versus raptors

label: All birds have four toes
claim: All birds, web-footed or not, have four toes on each foot, three in front and one behind (the Libyan ostrich set aside).
quote: In all birds alike, whether web-footed or not, the number of toes in each foot is four.

label: Only the wryneck has two toes in front and two behind
claim: The wryneck is the only bird whose toes are arranged two in front and two behind; all other birds have three in front and one behind.
quote: The arrangement of the toes is such as has been described in all birds with the exception of the wryneck. Here only two of the toes are in front, the other two behind

label: Fishes have at most four fins
claim: Fishes that are not broad and flat have four fins, two above and two below, and no fish ever has more than four.
quote: Fishes, unless, like the Batos and the Trygon, they are broad and flat, have four fins, two on the upper and two on the under side of the body; and no fish ever has more than these.
scope: fishes (Aristotle's 'fins' here are the paired pectoral and pelvic fins)

label: Selachians lack gill covers because their skeleton is cartilage
claim: In most fishes the gills are covered by opercula, but selachians (cartilaginous fishes) have none, because their skeleton is cartilaginous.
quote: These gills are in most fishes covered by opercula, but in the Selachia, owing to the skeleton being cartilaginous, there are no such coverings.

label: Selachians and the dolphin have an underslung mouth and turn on the back to feed
claim: In the dolphin and the selachians the mouth is on the underside, so they turn onto their backs to take their food.
quote: while in others, as the dolphin and the Selachia, it is placed on the under surface; so that these fishes turn on the back in order to take their food.

label: No fish and no footless animal has testicles
claim: No fish has testicles, either external or internal, and neither does any footless animal, including the serpents.
quote: No fish has testicles either externally or internally; as indeed have no apodous animals, among which of course are included the serpents.

label: The cetacean blow-hole serves to discharge sea-water taken in by the mouth
claim: Dolphins, whales and other cetaceans have no gills but have a lung, and their blow-hole serves to discharge the sea-water taken into the mouth while feeding.
quote: But dolphins and whales and all such Cetacea are without gills; and, having a lung, are provided with a blow-hole; for this serves them to discharge the sea-water which has been taken into the mouth.

label: Nature avoids the infinite and always seeks an end
claim: Nature avoids the infinite, because the infinite is unending and imperfect, and Nature always seeks an end; so spontaneously generated creatures cannot breed an endless series of new kinds.
quote: But Nature flies from the infinite, for the infinite is unending or imperfect, and Nature ever seeks an end.
scope: All of nature, applied here to the generation of animals

label: Stationary testaceans and attached animals have no sexes
claim: Animals that do not move about, such as testaceans (shelled molluscs and the like) and animals that live clinging to something, have no sexes, any more than plants do.
quote: But all those creatures which do not move, as the testacea and animals that live by clinging to something else, inasmuch as their nature resembles that of plants, have no sex any more than plants have
scope: Sessile animals: testaceans (bivalves, sea snails and the like) and attached animals (sponges, sea squirts, barnacles)

label: The male supplies the efficient cause of generation, the female the material
claim: The male and female are the first principles of generation: the male supplies the efficient (moving) cause and the female supplies the material.
quote: the male and female principles may be put down first and foremost as origins of generation, the former as containing the efficient cause of generation, the latter the material of it.

label: Castration changes nearly the whole form of a male toward the female
claim: When a male animal is castrated, although only the generative part is disabled, nearly its whole form changes so that it seems female or close to it.
quote: This is plain in the case of castrated animals, for, though only the generative part is disabled, yet pretty well the whole form of the animal changes in consequence so much that it seems to be female or not far short of it
scope: Castrated male animals (domestic livestock and men)

label: Fishes and serpents have no testes, only two spermatic ducts
claim: Fishes and serpents have no testes at all, only two spermatic ducts.
quote: some of them have not testes at all, as the classes of fish and of serpents, but only two spermatic ducts.

label: Birds and oviparous quadrupeds have internal testes near the loin
claim: All birds and all oviparous quadrupeds (lizards, tortoises and other scaly reptiles) have their testes inside the body near the loin, by the kidneys.
quote: this applies (among animals breathing air and having a lung) to all birds and oviparous quadrupeds. For all these have their testes internal near the loin
scope: Birds and oviparous quadrupeds (lizards, tortoises, crocodiles)

label: The uterus is always double
claim: The uterus is always double, just as the testes of the male are always two.
quote: The uterus is always double, just as the testes are always two in the male.
scope: All females with a uterus or its analogue, including crustaceans, cephalopods and larger insects

label: Animals with only ducts or internal testes copulate more quickly
claim: Animals that have no testes but only ducts, or that have internal testes, are all quicker in accomplishing copulation than animals with external testes.
quote: so those which have not testes but only ducts, or which have them indeed but internally, are all quicker in accomplishing copulation.
scope: Fishes, snakes, birds and oviparous quadrupeds compared with mammals with external testes

label: Seasonally breeding birds' testes swell in the breeding season and shrink after
claim: Birds' testes are much enlarged at the time of copulation, and in birds that pair at one season of the year they become so small afterwards as to be almost indiscernible.
quote: for their testes are much enlarged at the time of copulation, and all those which pair at one season of the year have them so small when this is past that they are almost indiscernible

label: Hedgehogs copulate standing upright because of their spines
claim: Hedgehogs do not mount the female from behind like other quadrupeds but copulate standing upright, because of their spines.
quote: for the hedgehog does not, like the other quadrupeds, mount upon the back of the female, but they conjugate standing upright because of their spines.

label: Cartilaginous fishes and vipers bear live young from eggs formed inside
claim: Cartilaginous fishes and vipers first produce eggs internally and then bring forth their young alive.
quote: But the cartilaginous fish and the vipers produce their young alive externally, but first produce eggs internally.
scope: Selachians (cartilaginous fishes: sharks and rays) and vipers

label: Ovoviviparous animals keep their eggs inside because they are cold
claim: Cartilaginous fishes and vipers do not lay their eggs outside because they are of a cold nature, which leaves the egg-shell soft and unprotected.
quote: It is because they are of a cold nature, not hot as some assert, that they do not lay their eggs externally.

label: Elephant and hedgehog have internal testes because their skin is unsuitable
claim: The testes are internal in the elephant and the hedgehog, because their skin is not suited to form a separate protective covering (scrotum) for them.
quote: For the same reason they are internal in the elephant and hedgehog, for the skin of these, too, is not well suited to keep the protective part separate.
scope: Elephants and hedgehogs, alongside cetaceans, birds and scaly reptiles

label: Cephalopods copulate mouth to mouth with arms entwined
claim: Cephalopods copulate by entwining at the mouth, pushing against one another and enfolding their arms.
quote: The cephalopoda entwine together at the mouth, pushing against one another and enfolding their arms.

label: The octopus arm inserted in the female's funnel is not a generative organ
claim: The arm that the male octopus inserts into the female's funnel serves only for attachment and is not an organ useful for generation, being outside the male's seminal passage.
quote: is only for the sake of attachment, and it is not an organ useful for generation, for it is outside the passage in the male and indeed outside the body of the male altogether.
scope: Octopus (poulp) and other cephalopods with a hectocotylus

label: Fleas, flies and cantharides arise from putrefying matter
claim: Some insects, such as fleas, flies and cantharides, do not come from parents but from putrefying matter, and although they unite and generate, they produce only a scolex (larva), not a creature of their own kind.
quote: these insects do not come into being from animals but from putrefying matter, liquid or solid; such are fleas, flies, and cantharides.
scope: Fleas, flies and blister beetles (cantharides); gnats and similar insects said to arise without any union

label: In most mating insects the female is larger than the male
claim: In most insects that copulate, the female is larger than the male.
quote: In most of those which unite the female is larger than the male.

label: In most insects the female inserts a part into the male
claim: In most insects the male does not insert any part into the female; instead the female inserts a part of herself from below upwards into the male.
quote: In most cases the male does not insert any part into the female, but the female from below upwards into the male

label: Resemblances to ancestors can skip generations
claim: Children may resemble remote ancestors from whom nothing has come to them, since resemblances recur after an interval of generations.
quote: Further, children are like their more remote ancestors from whom nothing has come, for the resemblances recur at an interval of many generations
scope: Humans, with the example of a woman of Elis and an Ethiopian

label: Mutilated parents do not always have mutilated young
claim: The young of mutilated parents are not always mutilated, just as young are not always like their parents.
quote: And the young of mutilated parents are not always mutilated, just as they are not always like their parents
scope: Animals and humans with acquired injuries

label: Semen does not come from all parts of the body
claim: Semen is not drawn from every part of the parent's body, contrary to those who explain inheritance that way.
quote: Into this we must next inquire, since it is plain that the semen is not secreted from all the parts.

label: Large animals have few young, small animals many
claim: Large animals have few young and small animals have many.
quote: A further proof that it is not a waste-product, but rather a secretion, is the fact that the large animals have few young, the small many.

label: Humans gain half their adult height in about the first five years
claim: In human beings the body gains in about the first five years half the height that it gains in all the rest of life.
quote: for in about five years, in the case of human beings at any rate, the body seems to gain half the height that is gained in all the rest of life.

label: Fat people are less fertile because the secretion turns to fat
claim: Fat people, women as well as men, are less fertile than others, because in the well-nourished the secretion being concocted turns to fat instead of semen.
quote: And fat people, women as well as men, appear to be less fertile than others from the fact that the secretion when in process of concoction turns to fat with those who are too well-nourished.
scope: Humans; also fat he-goats and luxuriant vines

label: Semen is a secretion of useful nutriment in its last stage
claim: Semen is a secretion (residue) of useful nutriment in its final stage, not a waste-product of the body.
quote: From what has been said, it is clear that semen is a secretion of useful nutriment, and that in its last stage, whether it is produced by all or no.

label: Semen and menstruation begin at the same age
claim: Semen begins to appear in males at the same time of life as the menstrual flow begins in females, together with the change of voice and the development of the breasts.
quote: For the semen begins to appear in males and to be emitted at the same time of life that the catamenia begin to flow in females

label: Among viviparous animals females are smaller because of menstruation
claim: Among the viviparous animals females are smaller than males, because the secretion that would build the body is discharged as menstrual fluid, and this is the only class that menstruates.
quote: the same cause accounts for the fact that the bulk of the body is smaller in females than in males among the vivipara, since this is the only class in which the catamenia are discharged from the body.

label: The female is a kind of impotent male, unable to concoct semen
claim: The female is, as it were, an impotent male: she is female through an incapacity to concoct the final nutriment into semen.
quote: the woman is as it were an impotent male, for it is through a certain incapacity that the female is female, being incapable of concocting the nutriment in its last stage into semen
scope: Females of all animals with two sexes, especially women

label: All directly viviparous animals menstruate, though less than women
claim: All animals that are viviparous without first producing eggs (man and the viviparous quadrupeds) have a menstrual discharge, unless defective like the mule, though the discharge is not as abundant as in women.
quote: all these have the catamenia, unless they are defective in development as the mule, only the efflux is not abundant as in women.
scope: Humans and viviparous quadrupeds (placental mammals); the mule as an exception

label: Menstruation usually begins when the breasts have risen two fingers' breadth
claim: Menstruation generally begins in girls when the breasts have risen two fingers' breadth.
quote: for it is when they have risen two fingers’ breadth that the catamenia generally begin.

label: Nothing material from the male need enter the embryo; he imparts motion and form
claim: Nothing material from the male needs to become part of the embryo; what comes from him acts only by imparting motion and form, as the medical art cures a patient.
quote: It is plain then that it is not necessary that anything at all should come away from the male, and if anything does come away it does not follow that this gives rise to the embryo as being in the embryo, but only as that which imparts the motion and as the form

label: A hen producing wind-eggs can be made fertile by treading while the egg is yellow
claim: If a hen producing wind-eggs is trodden by a cock before the egg has begun to whiten, while it is still all yolk, the eggs become fertile instead of wind-eggs.
quote: For if a hen-bird is in process of producing wind-eggs and is then trodden by the cock before the egg has begun to whiten and while it is all still yellow, then they become fertile instead of being wind-eggs.
scope: Domestic fowl and other birds that lay wind-eggs (unfertilized eggs)

label: A hen trodden by a second cock while the egg is yellow bears chicks like the second
claim: If a hen is trodden by a second cock while her eggs are still yolk, the whole brood of chicks turns out like the second cock.
quote: And if while it is still yellow she be trodden by another cock, the whole brood of chicks turn out like the second cock.

label: In oviparous fishes only the eggs reached by the milt are fertilized
claim: In oviparous fishes the male sprinkles milt over the eggs after they are laid, and only the eggs the milt reaches are fertilized.
quote: When the female has laid her eggs, the male spinkles the milt over them, and those eggs are fertilized which it reaches, but not the others

label: In all animals that move about the sexes are separate
claim: In all animals that can move about, the sexes are separate, one individual male and another female of the same species, whereas in plants they are combined.
quote: In all animals which can move about, the sexes are separated, one individual being male and one female, though both are the same in species, as with man and horse.
scope: Locomotory animals (contrasted with plants and sessile animals)

label: Generation makes kinds eternal as species, not as individuals
claim: Animals generate because a living thing cannot be eternal as an individual but can be eternal as a species, which is why there is always a race of men, animals and plants.
quote: Now it is impossible for it to be eternal as an individual (though of course the real essence of things is in the individual)— were it such it would be eternal — but it is possible for it as a species.

label: Animals with blood are larger than bloodless ones, and mobile larger than fixed
claim: Taken generally, animals with blood are larger than bloodless animals, and animals that move about are larger than those that stay fixed.
quote: Therefore, taking a general view, we may say that sanguinea are of greater size than bloodless animals, and those which move about than those which remain fixed.
scope: Animals with blood (roughly vertebrates) versus bloodless animals (invertebrates); motile versus sessile animals

label: Eggs of fishes, crustaceans and cephalopods grow after being laid
claim: The eggs of birds and oviparous reptiles are complete when laid and do not grow, whereas the eggs of fishes, crustaceans and cephalopods are imperfect and increase in size after being laid.
quote: The eggs of others are imperfect; such are those of fishes, crustaceans, and cephalopods, for their eggs increase after being produced.
scope: Fishes, crustaceans and cephalopods, contrasted with birds and oviparous reptiles

label: All viviparous animals have blood
claim: All viviparous animals have blood, and animals with blood are either viviparous or oviparous unless altogether infertile.
quote: All the vivipara are sanguineous, and the sanguinea are either viviparous or oviparous, except those which are altogether infertile.
scope: Viviparous animals and animals with blood
